_what: Standards our code or docs NAME but do not follow, so they are deliberately not rows of the ONE register (public/app/cap-standards.js). tools/standards-scan.cjs fails a PR that cites a standard found on neither. kind: holds = a certificate a shop or a party holds, which we record as their attestation; research = compared or considered in a design or audit document, not adopted (a row the day a backlog item builds it); detail = one function honours a section of it, a line in that file and not a commitment a reader needs on the page. CMP-24, 2026-10-28, owner cb-compliance.
_fields: name = exactly as cited (the scan matches on letters and digits, case-blind) · kind · why = why it is not a row · cited = where it is named · since = the date it was listed

rows.name: ISO 9001
rows.why: A quality-management certificate a supplier or a shop holds. We record it as that party's attestation (instrument kind, verify, RAIDA cover); we do not run a quality-management system against it.

rows.name: ISO 9000
rows.why: The vocabulary behind ISO 9001; named beside it in the conformance and governance code as a certificate family a party holds.

rows.name: ISO 14001
rows.why: An environmental-management certificate a party holds; one of the attestation kinds a readiness check can ask for.

rows.name: ISO 45001
rows.why: An occupational health and safety certificate a party holds; an attestation kind, not a rule we implement.

rows.name: ISO 22000
rows.why: A food-safety management certificate a party holds; an attestation kind in the compliance library.

rows.name: ISO 22716
rows.why: Cosmetics good-manufacturing practice: a certificate a prospect's industry holds, named in prospect research only.

rows.name: ISO 31000
rows.why: The RAIDA register took the columns ISO 31000, MIL-STD-882E and FMEA agree on (the design doc marks the ISO 31000 parts we left out: a named risk owner, likelihood times severity, a treatment plan). A vocabulary source, not a risk process we run.

rows.name: XBRL
rows.why: Considered as a statutory mapping target in the ledger research; the chart maps to Schedule III lines (register row schedule-iii), not to the MCA XBRL taxonomy.

rows.name: ISO 7064
rows.why: The MOD 97-10 check digit an LEI carries. The 14 Oct audit found no checksum code; the LEI row says Partly for that reason. A row when the check is built (register row lei names the gap).

rows.name: ISO 13616
rows.why: IBAN. Bank-detail fields exist (lib/profile.js); no IBAN check digit is computed. Proposed as a Planned row by the 14 Oct audit, not adopted; a row when the check is built.

rows.name: ISO 3166-2
rows.why: Country subdivisions. The 14 Oct audit left it out on purpose: GST state codes sit in profilemap as data, not a standard we claim (the country row is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

rows.name: GS1 GDM
rows.why: GS1 Global Data Model starter attributes. Backlog only (CTR-50 merged into the product passport item CAT-17; PLT-9 deferred); no starter family is built. The GS1 rows that exist are GTIN, GPC, GDSN, Application Identifiers, EPCIS.

rows.name: GS1 Global Data Model
rows.why: The same item as GS1 GDM, written out in the platform backlog (PLT-9, deferred).

rows.name: GS1 Attribute Definitions
rows.why: A GS1 reference document listed as a reading item (DOC-24, deferred); nothing is built against it.

rows.name: GS1 Digital Link
rows.why: A GTIN, lot and expiry as a web address. Proposed as a Planned row by the 14 Oct audit, not adopted; the QR we draw today is register row iso18004-qr. A row the day the encoder ships.

rows.name: ISO 22301
rows.why: Business-continuity certification a UAE e-invoicing service provider must hold to be accredited. Named in the entry plan as a cost of becoming one, which we decided not to do.

rows.name: ISO 44001
rows.why: Collaborative business relationships. The contract stage words were taken from the practitioner bodies that cite it; nothing is implemented or certified against it.

rows.name: ISO/IEC 5055
rows.why: Automated source-code quality (CISQ). The maintainability pack names it as the standard the CodeQL and readability checks approximate; not measured against it.

rows.name: ISO/IEC 27701
rows.why: Privacy information management, the extension of ISO 27001. The record of processing and the impact assessment drafts took their record shape from its controls; no privacy management system is run or certified, and the drafts await the owner's sign-off (owner action O7). The law rows are ae-pdpl-ropa and the privacy rows per country.

rows.name: ISO/IEC 42001
rows.why: AI management system, organisation level. Reference only until a customer asks (the pack says so).

rows.name: RFC 3986
rows.why: One function percent-encodes an object key the way the object store signs it (unreserved characters kept). A line inside lib/storage-object.js, not a page commitment.

rows.name: RFC 5321
rows.why: One comment: the local part of an e-mail address is case-sensitive per the mail standard, whatever most servers do. A detail of one route, not a page commitment.
